title: En el mercado — at the market
summary: Ana buys vegetables and haggles a little. Prices, quantities and the courtesies that go round them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.translation: Good morning. What can I get you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Dos euros el kilo. Están muy buenos hoy.
lines.translation: Two euros a kilo. They are very good today.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Póngame dos kilos, por favor. Y un kilo de cebollas.
lines.translation: Give me two kilos, please. And a kilo of onions.

lines.speaker: B
lines.translation: Anything else? I have very good potatoes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.translation: No, thank you. How much is it altogether?

lines.speaker: A
lines.translation: Here you are. Thank you very much.

vocabulary.meaning: what can I get you? (literally: what shall I put for you?)
a kilo — prices are given per kilo, not per item
and fifty — how cents are said after the euros
thank YOU — the shopkeeper's reply to gracias

questions.explain: dos kilos de tomates y un kilo de cebollas

questions.q: How much are the tomatoes per kilo?
What else does the seller offer her?
How does the seller answer 'muchas gracias'?
questions.explain: A usted — 'thank YOU'. Common in shops and markets.
